name: Lava Temple, Lahore Fort
significance: A small Hindu shrine standing inside the walls of Lahore Fort, dating to the Sikh period and dedicated to Lava. It sits on Pakistani government property and is looked after by the Pakistan Hindu Council.
story: Lahore is said to take its name from Lava, son of Rama and Sita, who founded it as Lavapuri while his twin brother Kusha founded Kasur.

name: Mansehra Shiva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple about 15 km from Mansehra, rebuilt in the 1830s by the Raja of Jammu around a lingam reported to be some two thousand years old. Sealed from 1948, it became accessible again in 1998 and has been partially restored by Pakistani Hindus, who gather here for Shivaratri.

name: Valmiki Mandir, Lahore
significance: A temple to the sage Valmiki on Bhim Street in the Neela Gumbad quarter of Anarkali, held locally to be about twelve centuries old. With the Krishna Temple it is one of only two functioning Hindu temples left in Lahore; courts returned it from private occupants to public custodianship and it was restored in 2022 under the Pakistan Hindu Council and the Evacuee Trust Property Board.

name: Kalibari Mandir, Peshawar
significance: One of the few surviving Hindu temples in Peshawar, in the Cantonment, and among the very few in daily use — pilgrims come to it from across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Durga Puja is its principal festival. Renovation from 2017 added a langar hall and repaired the structure; the Pakistan Hindu Council administers it.

name: Shivala Teja Singh Temple
significance: A shivala in Sialkot raised by Sardar Teja Singh, sealed at Partition in 1947 and partly demolished by vandals in 1992. After 72 years shut it was reopened in 2019, renovated by the Pakistani government and handed to the Pakistan Hindu Council.

name: Ramapir Temple, Tando Allahyar
significance: A temple to Ramdev Pir founded in the British period, whose annual Ramapir Mela is reckoned the second-largest Hindu pilgrimage in Pakistan.
story: A local Hindu vowed to hold a Rama Pir mela if he were granted a child; when the wish was answered he carried an earthen lamp 460 km from the original shrine at Ramdevra in Rajasthan and built this temple around it.

name: Chandragup
deity: Shiva, worshipped here as Baba Chandrakup
significance: A mud volcano in Hingol National Park venerated by Hindus as an embodiment of Shiva under the name Baba Chandrakup, and a station of the four-day Hinglaj Yatra held each April alongside the nearby Hinglaj Mata Temple.
story: Pilgrims hold that the Hinglaj Mata temple may be entered only after homage has first been paid to Baba Chandrakup.

name: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Karachi
significance: The only surviving Swaminarayan temple in Pakistan, spread over more than 32,000 square yards on M. A. Jinnah Road in central Karachi; Gujarati merchants built a Swaminarayan shrine here in the 1890s, and the walled complex also shelters a gurdwara used by the city's Sikhs.

name: Shree Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple, Karachi
significance: A historic underground Shiva temple at Clifton in Karachi, reached by two staircases near the Jehangir Kothari Parade and descending six levels to a marble courtyard floor and a freshwater spring inside the cave. Its Shivratri observance draws some 25,000 pilgrims.

name: Samadhi of Ranjit Singh
deity: Funerary urns of Maharaja Ranjit Singh
patron: Kharak Singh; completed by Duleep Singh
style: Sikh with Hindu and Islamic elements
significance: A 19th-century Sikh shrine in Lahore holding the funerary urns of Maharaja Ranjit Singh along with the ashes of four Hindu queens who became sati and seven concubines. Begun by his son Kharak Singh in August 1839 and finished by his youngest son Duleep Singh in 1848, it was the last great state-funded building of independent Punjab before the British annexation of 1849; gilded domes and frescoes of the Sikh gurus and scenes from the Hindu epics cover it.
